newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Chinese say on track to revive Nigeria rail system.
newsitem.headline: Chinese say on track to revive Nigeria rail system.

text.p: China's rehabilitation of Nigeria's dilapidated railways will be completed by the target of October 1998, a Chinese official said on Thursday.
Nigeria and China signed a $520 million contract in 1995 for state-run China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation to overhaul the railways, deliver locomotives and provide technical expertise.
Zhang Zhongmin of the Chinese embassy in Lagos told Reuters the first phase had been completed and some 1,000 Chinese engineers to start the second phase would arrive in February.

"We plan to complete before time or meet the target date of overhauling the rail system by October 1998. Then we will pass it on to Nigeria just when the military government hands over power to the civilians," he added.
Military ruler General Sani Abacha has said he will hand power to a democratically-elected president on October 1, 1998.

Sino-Nigerian relations have been strong since Africa's most populous nation became an international pariah in 1995 over the hanging of writer Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight minority rights activists on murder charges.
Nigeria needs Chinese support to stave off any move in the United Nations Security Council for sanctions over alleged human rights abuses.
Half the contract sum was paid off by mid-1996 as Nigeria reaped a windfall from higher crude oil prices.

Zhang said 50 locomotives for the Nigerian tracks were being built in China under the second phase of the project. "In fact, the engineers have constructed four of the locomotives which are already on their way. They will be used to test-run some of the constructed tracks."
Other parts of the project include delivery of remaining locomotives and providing 100 Chinese engineers to manage the rail system for at least three years, he said.

Zhang said the first phase, begun last April and completed in October, involved surveying and designing of track: "The entire rail tracks had either been buried under water, soil, heaps of refuse or totally gone rotten."
Nigerian railways have been in ruins over a lack of funding, with tracks unused and locomotives disabled. The government believes overhauling the sector would help revive the economy.
